bull.b: Rapid growth in both total revenue and AI customer ARR indicates expanding demand for DigitalOcean’s infrastructure and platform services. The acceleration, record ARR additions, and higher-value AI workloads could strengthen the company’s growth profile over the next several quarters.

Broad adoption across compute, inference, databases, storage, and other services can deepen customer relationships and increase spending as workloads scale. Multi-product usage also supports retention and makes the platform more embedded in customers’ application operations.

Strong operating cash generation provides internal funding for capacity expansion while reducing reliance on external capital. Positive free cash flow, despite uneven conversion, gives DigitalOcean flexibility to support growth and absorb some investment requirements.

bear.b: The sharp recent decline in net and EBITDA margins indicates that growth is not yet translating consistently into reported profitability. Sustained compression would reduce earnings resilience and leave less cash available for reinvestment, debt service, or shareholder returns.

Greater industry supply and improving compute efficiency could lower pricing for infrastructure and AI workloads over time. If prices normalize faster than utilization and product mix improve, revenue growth, ARR per megawatt, and margins could all face structural pressure.

Upcoming note repayment creates a material funding requirement, while the equity program could dilute existing shareholders if used. These financing actions may constrain capital allocation and increase dependence on continued operating performance during capacity expansion.
